title: Evacuation Route Message
description: WebSocket message carrying a hazard-weighted evacuation route for one worker. Coordinates are in the ship-visual system (Z-up, 60m x 20m x 14m true scale, see the coordinate_system property and ADR-010); the frontend applies only the Z-up to Y-up axis swap at render time. See docs/12_EVACUATION_ROUTE_SPEC.md and ADR-009.

route_id.description: ULID. A new id is issued only when the route is actually replaced (see spec 3.4).

route_status.description: safe: no hazard crossing. degraded: crosses level1/level2. no_safe_route: only a minimum-risk path through a level3 zone exists — the path is still returned, never hidden. unavailable: cannot compute.

coordinate_system.description: Ship-scale coordinate system (Z-up), 60m x 20m x 14m, mapped with the uniform TRUE SCALE preset. The FILL preset must never be used for route geometry because its non-uniform scaling distorts distance and would pick the wrong nearest exit. The frontend applies only the Z-up to Y-up axis swap, no further ratio mapping. See docs/12_EVACUATION_ROUTE_SPEC.md section 2.4 and ADR-010.

assumed_level_id.description: Scaffold level the worker is ASSUMED to be on. UWB positioning is 2D, so this is an assumption, not a measurement. The dashboard must surface it.

entry_nav_node_id.description: Graph node the worker position was snapped to.

total_cost.description: Sum of length_m * traverse_factor * hazard_multiplier over the route.

hazard_multiplier_max.description: Worst hazard multiplier on the chosen route. 1.0 means hazard-free.

waypoints.description: Ordered path. seq 0 is the worker's actual measured position, not a graph node.

nav_node_id.description: null for seq 0 (the worker's raw position).

then.description: safe/degraded/no_safe_route all carry a renderable path. no_safe_route still returns the minimum-risk path — never hide it (spec 3.3).
